text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: gpu-cluster-oom-rate > 10/min on us-west1-d-gpu-pool. Severity: P1. Paging on-call.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident #PD-4821 fired (gpu-memory-pressure). Notified: sarah-oncall.

sarah-oncall: Acked. I'm on it, switching to incident channel. Anyone nearby who patched kvcache last night?

miguel: I'm around. I ran the kvcache rollout at 02:10 UTC but it looked fine in canaries.

sarah-oncall: Logs show repeated CUDA OOM on multiple nodes, starting ~2067890115. Sample from node gpu-uw1-n04:
```
[2026-03-14T10:22:01Z] inference-server[pid=2211]: cuMemAlloc failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY size=4831838208
[2026-03-14T10:22:01Z] inference-server[pid=2211]: runtime error: failed to allocate KV cache, evicting session
```

ryan: Confirmed similar lines on gpu-uw1-n05. Memory pressure metric shows sustained 98-100% GPU memory utilization on that pool.

jess: Customer-facing note: a few dedicated customers in that pool may be reporting timeouts. I can start comms once we know scope.

sarah-oncall: Quick mitigation plan: 1) scale down batch_size at routing layer for this pool to 1, 2) disable heavy KV cache for new requests, 3) cordon+drain the two worst nodes and restart the inference container, 4) enable fallback route to cpu-quantized model for non-low-latency tiers. Migrating now.

miguel: Running commands to reduce batching and evict heavy sessions:
```
# lower global max batch size for us-west1-d-gpu-pool
kubectl -n inference patch config gpu-pool-config --type merge -p '{"spec":{"maxBatchSize":1}}'
# disable kv cache for new sessions
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/inference-router DISABLE_KV_CACHE=true
```

platform-ops: Starting cordon/drain on gpu-uw1-n04 and gpu-uw1-n05, will evict pods to other healthy nodes. If other nodes also saturated, we'll trigger autoscale fallback.

pagerduty-bot: sarah-oncall acknowledged the page at 2067890132. Escalation to SEV2 policy in 8m if not resolved.

ryan: After reducing batch_size, token-per-second dropped ~40% on that pool, memory pressure eased to ~75% on survivors. However two nodes still hit spikes during long-chat sessions. Draining now.

jess: I'm drafting a quick customer note: "We observed transient GPU memory pressure in a dedicated pool affecting latency for certain requests. We implemented throttling and fallbacks; customers on dedicated capacity may see slightly higher latency while we stabilize." Want to confirm before sending to customer list.

sarah-oncall: Good. Miguel, after drains finish, let's restart inference containers with --kv-cache-size=64MB and force GC on startup. Also schedule a short config rollback of yesterday's kvcache change if we see correlation.

miguel: Restart done on gpu-uw1-n04 at 2067890198, container back up. Logs now show no immediate cuMemAlloc failures.

platform-ops: Node gpu-uw1-n05 drained and rebooted (OOM kill evidence). Re-added to pool at 2067890240.

ryan: Running post-change watch: 20m window of stable memory use required before closing. Current watched metric: allocation failures = 0 in last 5m, GPU mem avg ~68%.

pagerduty-bot: Incident auto-escalation canceled; issue acknowledged and mitigation in progress.

jess: Sent preliminary customer note to affected accounts (Customer Success copied). No escalations yet.

sarah-oncall: Triage notes for handoff: probable root cause = bursty long-chat KV cache growth interacting with default kvcache rollout; mitigation = reduced batching, kv cache limits, node drains, restart with smaller kv cache. Next steps for postmortem: collect full allocator traces, correlate kvcache rollout flag toggles, evaluate autoscale thresholds for dedicated pools, add proactive alert for kvcache growth rate.

miguel: I'll open a follow-up ticket (ENGINF-8349) and attach the kube events/log snippets.

ryan: Handoff to night on-call @sarah-oncall -> @miguel at 2067890280. Leaving monitoring watch for 2 more hours.

sarah-oncall: Thanks team. I'll keep the incident open until we hit 20m stable and then convert to post-incident thread.

incident-bot: Incident PD-4821 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
